findings.claim: The new InspectMainAgent method carries two stacked doc comments: the port-level paragraph and then a second 'InspectMainAgent returns...' line. This reads as duplicated documentation on one method; merging them would be clearer.

The settings import is placed between the standard library imports (errors and path/filepath) in the same block rather than grouped with the other module imports, which breaks the import grouping used in missing_test.go in the same change.

fakeHooks.InspectMainAgent returns the shared inspectErr, so a test that sets inspectErr to exercise the Inspect failure path also makes the main-agent inspection fail. The two failure paths cannot be set apart, and an error on the hooks inspection can be masked or confused with the key inspection error. A separate agentErr field would keep them independent.

evidence: The production change in claude.go removes the type assertion, so every HookInstaller now answers the key; the call sites compile only if all implementers gained the method, and the test fakes in the diff were all updated.
The updated call-order expectation in TestClaudeAdapterHandsThePortTheFileAndTheBinaryOfItsRoot matches the new fake that records inspect-agent calls after install, install and status.
No behavioral defect found in the production code; findings are readability and test-fake concerns only.
